idle: (He offers the person next to him a cruller. They accept.)
bad_ice: (He looks at the ice the way he looks at dough that won't rise.)
wet_ice: (He lifts his boots off the wet floor and keeps them there.)
cold: (He turns his collar up and holds the coffee with both hands.)
hungry: (He opens a paper bag. It is his own crullers. He is not hungry for anyone else's.)
long_line: (He waits. He waits like a man who gets up at 3:30 every morning.)
bored: (He folds a napkin into a very neat square.)
goal: (He claps once, quietly, and looks around to make sure nobody saw.)
leaving_happy: (He leaves a cruller on the seat for whoever comes next.)
leaving_angry: (He takes his crullers with him. All of them.)

beer_league: (Back row. Coffee. Coat on the next seat.)
(He sees a camera and pulls his toque down.)
stick_and_puck: (Early. Nobody else here. He seems content.)

first.say: (A quiet man in a flour-dusted jacket nods at you. He hands you a cruller. That appears to be the whole introduction.)

first_name.say: Donnie. (He nods a second time. You get the sense that two nods is a lot.)

first_1996.say: (He looks at you for a long time. Then he gently takes the cruller back and puts it in his pocket.)

first_eat.say: (You eat it. It is the best cruller you have ever had. He watches you realise this, and very nearly smiles.)

grumpy.say: (He looks at the coffee. He looks at you. He puts a cruller back in the bag instead of handing it over.)

options.text: I'm sorry, Donnie. I'll do better.

back_row.say: (Back row, coffee in hand. He sees you and moves his coat off the seat next to him. Around here, that is an honour.)

cake_no_greet.say: (He nods. Then he puts a small cake on the bench beside you. It says OK in blue icing. You are forgiven, apparently.)

options.text: What do you think of the place?
Could I buy half a dozen?
Would you help me run my bench?
I'd like to offer you a contract.

job.say: Four a.m. (He holds up four floury fingers, then mimes rolling dough, then mimes going back to bed at one in the afternoon.)

events.say: (He points at the back row. Then at the canteen. Then he shrugs. A seat, a coffee, and nobody looking. That is the whole plan.)

gossip.say: (He opens the box. Twelve crullers. The lid says SHAUNA in marker. A second box says RONNIE. You are looking at a standing order system older than your mortgage.)

rink.say: (He taps the snack bar counter, then the coffee machine, then gives the coffee machine a look you would not want to receive.)

options.text: It's been fixed up, hasn't it?

rink_better.say: (He runs a hand along the new counter. He nods. Two nods.)

buy.say: Nine. (He holds out a white bag. It is warm. It is somehow still warm.)

path_coach.say: (He says nothing. On Saturday he is at the end of your bench in a flour-dusted jacket, and he does not say why, and you learn not to ask.)

path_gm.say: (He says nothing. The next morning there is a cake on your office desk. It says NO, in very neat icing. It is delicious.)

do.note: Donnie Delorme's reply to your contract offer: a cake that says NO. It was delicious.
